I think it's okay for intent to be captured from work trees that never land. I think most work trees will land, and if something, well, let me just leave it at that. I think it's okay for intent to land. I'm also now rethinking whether it makes sense for the sessions to, I'm wondering if I should force the sessions to always be a separate repo. The sessions record can still have a remote, and one or more people can still merge and push and pull the sessions for, I'm thinking for traceability and, after the fact recording. So I think I want to reverse that decision and make it so that the record of sessions still is always a separate repository, because I think it's an easy mistake to make, and I just want to reduce the chances of some stuff leaking by accident through that mechanism. But everything else I think makes sense. The only other thing I wonder is that intent is really supposed to be about the project intent and less about the configuration of the system of recording the intent and the research and experiments and all that kind of stuff. And so I don't know if it really classifies as intent. Well, I mean, in a sense it is, but intent is really supposed to be more about the project, intent of the project itself. So I don't know if there's another way it can be stored, or maybe I just need to get over it, and that is a form of intent. I don't know. I guess I'm on the fence about that.
